text:
Margo: noticed small but reproducible data leak in console when switching orgs quickly. saved search from org A briefly shows rows from org B for ~200-400ms. steps to repro below.
Devon: omg, can you paste repro steps + browser/network logs?
Margo: steps: 1) login as user with access to both orgs 2) open insights -> saved search list 3) rapidly switch org via quick-switch header twice 4) observe rows flicker (org B rows show then replaced). saw in network: GET /api/console/savedsearches?org_id=orgA returned payload with orgB ids.
Sam: was this on canary or prod? any rollout flags?
Margo: saw on prod in us-east, but only after the console routing rollout (last week). no canary flag for the user.
Aria: @infra-bot can you pull router logs for those timestamps?
infra-bot: querying router logs for ts range 4387654300-4387654400... found 12 requests with header X-Org:orgA routed to service instance pool-1 then to pool-2 in same trace. adding link: https://internal/logs/4387654321
Devon: interesting — header X-Org seems to switch mid-trace. could be header mutation in the edge or proxy sticky session handing off to different route that has stale affinity tag.
Ivy: also check the request id propagation. we had a bug where route-tag wasn't copied into internal requests during prefetch.
Sam: can you grep for "route-tag" in proxy traces?
Margo: pasted sample proxy trace snippet:
```
[TRACE] req=abcd1234 src=console-fe -> edge-proxy: X-Org: orgA; Route-Tag: r=42
[TRACE] req=abcd1234 edge-proxy -> router: X-Org: orgB; Route-Tag: r=42
[TRACE] handler pool-2 fetched savedsearches with org_id=orgB
```
Devon: that looks like header flip at edge-proxy -> router hop. maybe our session-affinity cookie rewrite path triggers a header swap when cookie points to older tenant context.
Aria: could also be KV cache reuse at the runtime. route-tag r=42 might be reused across tenants if cache key omits org namespace.
Ivy: confirmed: cache key for saved-searches was `savedsearch:<user_id>:recent` without org. that explains orgB leakage if user has multi-org access. oof.
Sam: ok two possible causes: 1) edge-proxy header mutation 2) cache key missing org. which one is the root?
Margo: timeline: this repro only appeared after route-tag rollout last week. before that, savedsearch fetch always hit service directly. route-tag introduced prefetching and pooling. seems more likely cache key bug exposed by pooling.
Devon: assignable fix: prefix cache keys with org_id and ensure router preserves X-Org on internal hops. quick patch for caching in service is low-risk. router/edge fix harder.
Aria: agree. plan: (a) hotfix savedsearch service to include org in cache key and bust the cache for a minute, (b) add integration test for multi-org user scenario, (c) deeper audit of header propagation in proxy.
Margo: +1. can we also add telemetry alert so we detect any cross-org rows showing up? maybe a post-filter check emitting metric when returned org_id != requested org.
Ivy: cheap metric: increment `console.savedsearch.mismatched_org` when mismatch detected. we can surface in console dashboards.
Sam: I'll own rollout for the caching patch. target: 30-min patch and quick rollback plan if error rate spikes.
Devon: I'll take proxy trace audit and a small integration test.
Aria: I'll add the telemetry increment and dashboard tile. Ivy will add cache key change in PR.
Margo: thanks team. posting the minimal repro gist for QA: https://internal/gists/4387654321-repro.
Ivy: PR created: https://phabricator/PR/7890 — patch updates cache key and adds unit tests.
Sam: deployed patch to prod-canary 1/3 instances. monitoring for 5m.
infra-bot: canary deploy started at 4387654350. health checks green.
Sam: seeing no mismatched_org metrics in canary window. good so far.
Devon: continuing proxy audit; found one codepath in edge-proxy that overwrites headers when switching backend pools during a retry. creating follow-up ticket.
Aria: created telemetry dashboard: Console > Multi-org leaks > mismatched_org (last 1h). sharing link in #eng-observability.
Margo: after canary rollout to 100% and cache invalidation, can't repro locally or prod anymore. thanks all.
Sam: next steps: postmortem + include cache naming guidelines in README to avoid future org-agnostic keys.
Margo: leaving note for product: UX rollouts that change routing must be tested with multi-org users. they missed that matrix in rollout checklist. :thinking_face: 
Devon: adding that checklist item now. :white_check_mark:
Ivy: closing this thread once PR merges and router follow-up ticket is created.
Margo: PR merged, router ticket created: RT-1122. closing. :thumbsup:
